data.narrative:
eGenesis, a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Luhan Yang and George Church, has raised $250M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage private companies (Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit) and 3 public Biotech & Health comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two valuation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method uses the $250M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression, yielding $425M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of three private Biotech & Health companies at Series C, which stands at $3.8B, with a range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. A public-comp P/S approach cannot be applied due to the absence of revenue disclosure, common for private-stage companies. The public Biotech & Health sector median P/S is 5.5x across three tickers, but lacks target-specific revenue data.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $361M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The wide range reflects meaningful dispersion among peer valuations and methodological assumptions. Key uncertainties include the stability of peer multiples in a volatile biotech sector, the relevance of public-comp multiples to private-stage risk profiles, and eGenesis's position relative to the peer set on development stage and capital efficiency.
